steps.label: open the Tiles tab
steps.goal: the three tiles come first -- a room can only be assembled out of pieces the kit already has. The tab opens on your tiles, with New Tile + at the top
do: press 2
steps.recovery: if a text field has the keyboard the number types into it: press Escape first

steps.label: start the corner tile
steps.goal: a corner is where two solid sides meet. Without one a kit can only make corridors -- there is no way to close a room off
do: press N for a new tile
type a name like corner
press Enter
steps.recovery: Escape closes the name prompt without starting the tile

steps.label: floor it, then stand two walls at right angles
steps.goal: the floor is what gives the tile a size and edges, so it goes first. The second wall needs R to turn it a quarter before it can go flush against the NEXT side round -- that quarter turn is the whole difference between a corner and a doubled wall
do: walk to site/floor and press Enter
press Escape, walk to site/wall, press Enter
shift-arrow it flush against one side
press Enter for a second wall, press R to turn it a quarter
shift-arrow that one flush against an ADJACENT side
steps.recovery: if the second wall will not sit flush, it is probably not turned -- R again. If the arrows walk the list instead of the piece, press Escape then Enter

steps.label: does it read as a corner
steps.goal: before saving it: the two walls should meet, not overlap and not leave a gap at the join. This is the thing no checkpoint can answer and the reason the exercise is worth a person's time
do: orbit the camera and look at where the two walls meet
steps.recovery: if they overlap or leave a gap, say which, and say what flush landed on -- that is the report

steps.label: save the corner
steps.goal: saving is what puts it in the kit, and only what is in the kit can be stamped onto a map
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if it refuses, the message names what it objected to -- that message is the report

steps.label: start the wall tile
steps.goal: a plain run of wall -- one side solid, the other three open. Four of these and four corners is a room
do: press N
type a name like wall_run
press Enter
steps.recovery: if N did nothing, the previous tile may still be unsaved -- Cmd+S first

steps.label: floor it and flush ONE wall to one side
steps.goal: same shape as the corner minus the turned second wall. Flush is the last stop on the arrow ladder, so from centre it should be reachable without overshooting
do: walk to site/floor and press Enter
press Escape, walk to site/wall, press Enter
shift-arrow it flush against one side
steps.recovery: press J to change the step size if flush is hard to land on, then arrow again

steps.label: save the wall tile
steps.goal: two of the three in the kit
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if the count looks wrong the kit already shipped some tiles -- that is expected, this asks for more than were there

steps.label: start the door tile
steps.goal: a room you cannot walk into is a box. site/wall_doorway is the wall with the hole already in it, so the door tile is the wall tile with one piece swapped
do: press N
type a name like doorway
press Enter
steps.recovery: Cmd+S the previous tile first if N does nothing

steps.label: floor it and flush the doorway to one side
steps.goal: flushed exactly the way the plain wall was -- if the two sit differently, a doorway swapped into a wall run will not line up, and that misalignment is the single most likely defect this whole exercise exists to find
do: walk to site/floor and press Enter
press Escape, walk to site/wall_doorway, press Enter
shift-arrow it flush against one side -- the SAME side you used for the wall tile
steps.recovery: if you cannot find it in the list, press F and type doorway, then Enter to hand the keyboard back

steps.label: save the door tile
steps.goal: three tiles: corner, wall, door. That is enough vocabulary for a room
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if it refuses, the message names what it objected to

steps.label: go to the Compose tab and arm the wall tile
steps.goal: the Map stamps whatever is armed here. This is the step that connects the two halves of the exercise, and it is the one an author is least likely to guess
do: press 4
walk the list with up and down to your wall tile
press Enter to arm it
steps.recovery: the status line says which tile is armed -- if it says nothing was armed, the list selection is on something else

steps.label: lay the four walls
steps.goal: now the room. Four wall tiles for the sides -- leave the corners for the next step and leave one gap in a side for the door
do: press 1 for the Map tab
click to stamp the armed tile
press R or T to turn it so each side faces inward
lay four runs, leaving a gap at each corner and one gap for the door
steps.checkpoint: the map has tiles on it
steps.recovery: if a click places nothing, nothing is armed -- go back to 4 and press Enter on the tile

steps.label: close the four corners
steps.goal: the corner tile is the piece the whole first half was for. Each one needs a different quarter turn
do: press 4, walk to your corner tile, press Enter to arm it
press 1
stamp one into each corner, pressing R to turn it to face the right way
steps.checkpoint: the map has tiles on it
steps.recovery: if a corner will not sit where you want, say what it did instead -- refusing to overlap is correct, landing somewhere unexpected is not

steps.label: put the door in
steps.goal: the last piece, into the gap you left
do: press 4, walk to your door tile, press Enter to arm it
press 1
stamp it into the gap, turned to match the run it sits in
steps.checkpoint: the map has tiles on it
steps.recovery: if it will not go in the gap, the gap is probably the wrong size -- say what it refused with

steps.label: walk round it and say whether it is a room
steps.goal: the question the whole exercise is for. Not 'did the checkpoints pass' -- whether what is on screen reads as a room somebody could stand in
do: orbit the camera all the way round
look along each wall run for seams, gaps and doubled-up pieces
look at the doorway: is the hole where a person would walk through it
steps.recovery: everything that looks wrong here is the report, however small -- a seam at one corner and not the others is more useful than a general impression

steps.label: save the map
steps.goal: what you built is on disk in a form the game reads, as nine tile references rather than a hundred loose pieces
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if it refuses, the message names what it objected to -- that message is the report
